<Route path="/ade/merge-requests/[id]" />

Draft a change on a **branch** of its own, open a **merge request**, let reviewers approve it, and
merge it into the version line — all inside Apiome, with no Git repository to wire up.

A merge request does not add a second review or merge process. It brings together three things
Apiome already has:

- the **review** of the branch — reviewers decide on the [review page](../govern/reviews.mdx);
- a **merge session** — the same three-way merge as **Merge branches…**, with the same conflict list;
- the **classified diff** — what the branch changes, grouped as breaking, non-breaking and docs-only.

<Screenshot id="merge-request" alt="Merge request Add refund reason codes: feature/refund-reasons into main, the classified changes since the merge base, and the Status card ready to merge" />

<Flag name="FEATURE_GITLIKE" />

The **Merge requests** tab on Versions is one of the Git-like controls, which are switched off in
shipped builds — see [Turning on the Git-like controls](./version-control.mdx#turning-on-the-git-like-controls).
The REST API works without the switch; see [API](#api).

## Draft a change on a branch

A **version line** is the branch a version lives on — usually `main`. A **draft branch** starts from
the line's current tip:

1. **Open Versions** for the project and **choose the “Merge requests” tab**.
2. **Click “New draft branch”**.
3. Type a **Branch name**, for example `feature/refund-reasons`.
4. Choose the **Version line** to start from. The default branch is picked for you.
5. Optionally type a **Version label** for the branch's first version, for example `2.4.1`. Leave it
   empty to take the next patch version.
6. **Click “Create branch”**.

The branch gets a version of its own, a copy of the line's tip with its classes and paths. Edit that
version as you would any draft — in the Studio, on the canvas, or through the API. **The version line
does not change** until the branch is merged.

<Screenshot id="versions-merge-requests" alt="The Merge requests tab: one open merge request and two draft branches, each drafted off main" />

The tab lists merge requests by state — **Open**, **Merged** or **Closed** — and every draft branch
with the line it was drafted off and its tip.

## Open a merge request

1. **Click “Open merge request”** — on the tab, or beside a draft branch under **Draft branches**.
2. Choose the **Draft branch** and the line to **Merge into**. The line the branch was drafted off is
   picked for you.
3. Type a **Title**, for example `Add refund reason codes`, and an optional **Description**.
4. Tick one or more **Reviewers**. You cannot review your own merge request.
5. **Click “Open merge request”**.

Apiome requests a review of the branch's tip from the reviewers you chose, and they are notified as
for any review. If the tip already has an open review, that review is attached instead. A branch can
have one open merge request at a time.

## Review and merge

The merge request page has three tabs and a **Status** card:

- **Changes** — what the branch changes, compared with the **merge base** (the version the branch
  and the line last had in common). Comparing with the merge base shows only the branch's own changes,
  not everything the line gained since. **Plain diff** switches to a line diff of the two
  [documents](./versions.mdx#the-versions-document); when they are the same it says **Identical
  documents** instead.
- **Conflicts** — what the last merge session found; see [Resolve conflicts](#resolve-conflicts).
- **Review** — where the branch's review stands, with each reviewer's decision. **Click “Open the
  review”** to approve, request changes, suggest edits or discuss on the review page.

The **Status** card says **Ready to merge into main** or lists what is left. **Merge into main** is
enabled only when nothing is:

| Shown | Means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Request a review of the branch before merging.** | No review is attached, or it was withdrawn. | **Click “Request review of the current tip”**. |
| **The branch moved on after the review was requested.** | Someone added a version to the branch, so the review judged an older tip. | **Click “Request review of the current tip”**; the old review is withdrawn. |
| **N reviewer(s) have not decided yet.** | The review is in progress. | Wait for the reviewers. |
| **A reviewer requested changes.** | The review round is decided against. | Change the branch, then re-request the review on the review page. |
| **The branch changed after this review round was requested.** | The approvals were given to different content. | Re-request the review on the review page. |
| The approval policy's message | The project's [approval gate](../govern/reviews.mdx#turn-on-the-approval-gate) needs more approvals, or one from a given role. | Ask another reviewer. |
| **N conflicting path(s) with main.** | The last merge session found overlapping changes. | See [Resolve conflicts](#resolve-conflicts). |
| **The tip of main is published and immutable.** | The line's tip is a published version. | A tenant administrator ticks **Override published immutability** and types a **Reason**, which is recorded in the audit log. |

Then **click “Merge into main”**. Apiome runs a fresh merge session against the current tips and, when
it finds no conflicts, merges through the same path as **Merge branches…**: the line gets a new
version with both tips as parents, the project's compatibility gate applies, and the merge is recorded
on the [project activity timeline](./project-timeline.md). The merge request then reads **Merged**.

To give up instead, **click “Close merge request”**. The branch and its versions stay; the review is
withdrawn if you requested it or are an administrator.

## Resolve conflicts

**Click “Check for conflicts”** at any time to run a merge session against the current tips. A merge
that finds conflicts stops before changing anything and opens the **Conflicts** tab.

<Screenshot id="merge-request-conflicts" alt="The Conflicts tab: two schema paths changed on both feature/refund-reasons and main, in the merge conflict list" />

The list is the same one **Merge branches…** shows: each path changed on both the branch and the line.
A merge only ever applies a clean three-way result, so resolve a conflict by **editing the draft
branch** until the path no longer overlaps — for example, take over the line's definition of the
class and re-apply your change. The **Mine** / **Theirs** marks help you track which side each path
should keep. Then **click “Check for conflicts”** again.

A merge carries **class and property changes** — the schema components the merge session merges. Path
edits on the branch are not merged.

## API

Every step is available over REST, with or without the Git-like switch. The full reference is
[Merge requests](../reference/rest/merge-requests.md).

```http
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project}/draft-branches
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{ "name": "feature/refund-reasons", "base_branch": "main" }
```

```http
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project}/merge-requests
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{ "source_branch": "feature/refund-reasons", "title": "Add refund reason codes", "reviewers": ["<user-id>"] }
```

- `GET …/merge-requests/{id}` returns the branches' tips, the merge base, the review, the latest merge
  session with its conflicts, and `readiness` — `can_merge` and every blocker.
- `POST …/merge-requests/{id}/check` runs a merge session; `…/merge` merges (`409 mr-not-ready` with
  `blockers`, `409 mr-conflicts` with `conflicts`); `…/review` reviews the current tip; `…/close`
  closes.
- Creating a draft branch needs `versions:create`; opening, merging and closing need `versions:edit`;
  reading and checking need `versions:view`.
